rows.analogue_of: PSRS-D2D attack 1 (key computable from public values)
rows.attacker: eavesdropper with the full transcript, all certificates and the authority key
rows.evidence: tried the key schedule on all 32 public values: 0 matched; the key's only secret input is ss = ML-KEM.Decaps(dk_e, ct); dk_e is never sent

rows.attack: Past sessions after every long-term key leaks
rows.analogue_of: PSRS-D2D attack 2, P2AS-IoAV attack 2 (no forward secrecy)
rows.attacker: recorded transcript; later gets both vehicles' signing keys and the authority's key
rows.evidence: 7 leaked long-term secrets tried as decapsulation keys: 0 gave the key; initiator's ephemeral key erased after use: True
rows.control: with the ephemeral key (if it had been kept, as P2AS keeps static keys) the key IS recovered: True

rows.attack: Capture two vehicles, then forge a certificate
rows.analogue_of: PSRS-D2D attack 3 (authority keys from two certificates)
rows.attacker: full memory of two captured vehicles (all their keys and certificates)
rows.evidence: self-signed new certificate: rejected (bad certificate signature); grafted certificate: rejected (bad certificate signature); victim's certificate with attacker signature: rejected (initiator signature invalid); certificates are ML-DSA signatures by the authority: no equations in its secret to solve

rows.attacker: no valid credentials for the victim; can observe and replay traffic
rows.evidence: observed certificate, attacker's signature: rejected (initiator signature invalid); real message with swapped ephemeral key: rejected (initiator signature invalid); replay of a real message within the window: rejected (replayed nonce); replay 60 s later: rejected (stale timestamp); message from a revoked vehicle: rejected (peer certificate rejected: certificate revoked)

rows.attack: Man in the middle swaps the KEM ciphertext
rows.attacker: controls the channel; re-encapsulates to the initiator's ephemeral key

rows.evidence: different pseudonyms share an identifier (pseudonym or key): False; 24 16-byte windows shared across the two pseudonyms; 0 absent from another vehicle's message (would identify it); honest limit: two sessions under the SAME pseudonym (lifetime 300 s) are linkable: True; the rotation interval is the privacy setting
rows.control: the same test on two sessions under ONE pseudonym finds 3773 identifying windows, so it does detect linkable traffic

rows.attack: Offline password guessing from vehicle storage
rows.analogue_of: PSLAP attack 2 (password verifier in the OBU)
rows.attacker: full read-out of a vehicle's stored state
rows.evidence: stored vehicle state: ['authority_pk', 'authority_scheme', 'config', 'credentials', 'crl', 'kem', 'rng', 'scheme', 'seen_nonces']; no password or password-derived verifier exists to test guesses against

rows.attack: Quantum attacker breaks X25519 in hybrid mode
rows.analogue_of: Shor demo (ECC falls to a quantum computer)
rows.attacker: learns the X25519 shared secret (as Shor's algorithm would), plus the transcript
rows.evidence: with the X25519 secret and 20 candidate ML-KEM secrets: 0 matched; the key also needs the ML-KEM shared secret, which Shor's algorithm does not give
